title: Something Pressed Between the Leaves
sceneText:
Going through last year’s files, you come to a folio with no number on it.

It is not accounts. There are loose things inside it: two receipts, a copy of a contract, several notes written half through.

The hand on the notes is Hartmann’s.

When you reach the middle, something slides out from between the leaves.

A small sprig of a dried plant. Pressed very flat, the colour gone to pale brown, the edges whole. It was put in there carefully. It did not fall in by chance.

You hold it up to the light.

This folio is in this room. This room is cleaned by Elena. And the way the thing has been laid between the leaves says that whoever laid it there wanted it to stay flat.

choices.text: Go and ask her about it

effects.logEntry: You took the sprig to Elena and asked about it.

choices.resultText:
You find her in the afternoon and show her the sprig.

She looks at it once and says she does not know.

“I do not move what is inside when I clean,” she says. “With the folio I only wipe the cover.”

What she says may well be true. You have no way to tell.

When she has said it she waits a few seconds. You do not ask anything more, and she goes.

The folio was still in the same place the next day, with not a page moved.

choices.text: Put it back where it was

effects.logEntry: You put the sprig back between the same two pages.

choices.resultText:
You lay it back between the same two pages, squared to where it was, then close the folio and put it back on the shelf.

When you put it back you push it in half an inch further than it stood, because you would rather nobody saw at a glance that you had touched it.

You mention it to nobody.

Three days later you go past that shelf. The folio is still there.

Somebody has drawn it back out half an inch.
